title: attempted to add a product to the cart on ecommerce-playground.lambdatest.io
source_description: User can add a product to the cart from the product detail page and see the cart item count update
expected_result:
The run navigated to a LambdaTest eCommerce Playground product page (HTC Touch HD) and tried to use the purchase controls next to the quantity selector.
On the product page, the purchase buttons were labeled “OUT OF STOCK,” indicating the item was not available to add to the cart.
The automation clicked the teal button to the right of the quantity selector and then clicked the teal “OUT OF STOCK” button, but since the product was out of stock, this did not add anything to the cart.
After scrolling down, it attempted to click a “Popup” button/link in the product options area, but this did not lead to completing the intended shopping action (no add-to-cart/cart page confirmation is shown).
The run likely failed because the item could not be purchased (out-of-stock state), so the expected add-to-cart behavior could not occur even though the buttons were clicked.

title: attempted to open a specific product page on ecommerce-playground.lambdatest.io
source_description: User can open the cart dropdown and see the list of added items with their names and prices
expected_result:
The run was trying to navigate to a specific product page on the LambdaTest eCommerce Playground and interact with the product purchase area (click the large turquoise “OUT OF STOCK” button).
The automation did reach a product detail page where the product box showed “Availability: Out Of Stock” and two “OUT OF STOCK” buttons, indicating the target kind of UI was present.
However, the run failed partway through because required steps could not be executed: Step 2 and Step 21 reported “step file not found,” so the flow stopped before it could reliably complete the intended actions.
There was also a navigation mismatch: a later step intended to go to product_id=28, but the browser ended up on product_id=43 instead, suggesting the navigation didn’t go to the exact requested page (possibly due to a wrong link/redirect or the step not running as expected).
Because of the missing step definitions and the incorrect final product page, the requested click and any follow-up outcome (such as adding to cart or confirming a message) could not be completed or verified.
kane_objective: Stop immediately once confirmed. Do not navigate further.
